Ridge Valley opens its first public library branch

By Nina Kowalczyk

Ridge Valley celebrated the opening of its first public library branch on Saturday, drawing several hundred residents to a ribbon-cutting ceremony on the building's front steps.

The 12,000-square-foot facility includes a children's reading room, a maker space with 3D printers, and a quiet study wing overlooking the community garden.

"We've wanted this for over a decade," said branch manager Foster Diallo, who previously ran the county's bookmobile program.

The library will be open six days a week starting next month, with extended hours during the school year.
